Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
Comments: Affordability improved but still 2-5% GNI pc for data basket in African context [ITU](https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Statistics/Documents/publications/prices2022/ITU_Price_Brief_2022.pdf)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The originally cited 2022 ITU price-brief PDF is now a dead link. Note the original comment (2-5% GNI) is internally inconsistent with the stated 'Expensive (5-10%)' Value Name. ITU/World Bank data show Africa's regional median data-only mobile-broadband basket at roughly 4.5-4.9% of GNI per capita (2022-23), and a World Bank competition-reform document shows Benin-specific values clustering around 5.5-6.5% GNI per capita across recent years, consistent with the 'Expensive (5-10%)' band. Confirmed at 2, but flagged for human review to obtain the exact current-year Benin-specific ITU figure, as the primary source could not be verified directly.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited DataReportal figure (93.6%) is total mobile connections/SIMs, not unique subscribers, and the variable explicitly requires unique subscriber penetration. GSMA's Benin report, using ARCEP end-2023 data, estimates unique mobile subscribers at 8.5 million, a 67% penetration rate — this falls in the 55-69% band. Changed from 5 to 4.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
Comments: Law No. 2017-20 Digital Code enacted, APDP DPA established [DLA Piper](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?t=law&c=BJ)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: DLA Piper confirms Law No. 2017-20 (digital code) and the APDP authority. Beyond mere establishment, APDP's own 2025 activity report documents active, ongoing enforcement: 782 control/litigation cases handled, 20 privacy complaints instructed, 64 compliance inspection missions, and financial sanctions issued for non-compliance. This sustained enforcement record supports the 'mature framework with active enforcement' tier. Changed from 4 to 5.

Definition: The maturity of the country's technology startup ecosystem, based on the number of tech startups, venture capital activity, accelerators/incubators, and the presence of a supportive ecosystem. Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited GSMA press release does not actually assess the startup ecosystem. Evidence found: e-mobility startup Spiro raised $50M in 2024 (52% of Francophone Africa's total funding that year) and later rounds up to $215M; Gozem raised a $30M Series B in 2025; a state-backed incubation campus (Sèmè City) and several hubs are active. This is beyond 'emerging' (1-2 hubs, very limited funding) and matches 'Developing' (growing startup base, regular funding rounds, several hubs). However, most large deals are foreign-led/headquartered ventures and Benin ranks 118th of 125 on the Global VC/PE Country Attractiveness Index, so 'Established' ($50M+ broadly distributed local ecosystem) is not yet supported. Changed from 2 to 3.

revision_notes: Re-checked committers.top: the current listing (data refreshed 2026) reports 2,160 total registered GitHub users located in Benin (with at least one follower), which is higher than the <1,000 implied by the original comment and could arguably fall in the 'Developing' band (1,000-10,000). However, this is a single aggregator source that does not distinguish active professional developers from casual/student accounts, so per instructions we do not upgrade on this alone. Left at 2 and flagged for human review with a request for a second, corroborating source (e.g. Google Developer Groups, Stack Overflow, AfriLabs).

revision_notes: The cited article's EGDI value (0.4264) is actually the 2022 UN E-Government Survey figure, mislabelled in the row as '2024' data.
